"**Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)**" is a song performed and co-written by American singer-songwriter Christopher Cross as the main theme for the 1981 film _Arthur_.
It was recognized as the year's Best Original Song at both the 54th Academy Awards and 39th Golden Globe Awards.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-British_Hit_Singles_&_Albums-3)

# Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)
A commercial success in the United States, it reached the top of both the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and Hot Adult Contemporary charts in October 1981, remaining at the top of the Hot 100 for three consecutive weeks. The song topped the VG-lista chart in Norway and was a top-ten hit in several other countries.

# Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)
## Background
[edit]
The song was written in collaboration between Cross, Burt Bacharach, and Bacharach's frequent writing partner and future wife Carole Bayer Sager. A fourth writing credit went to Liza Minnelli's ex-husband, Australian songwriter Peter Allen,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-British_Hit_Singles_&_Albums-3) a frequent collaborator with Bayer Sager. The line in the chorus "When you get caught between the moon and New York City" was taken from an unreleased song written by Allen and Bayer Sager.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-4) Allen came up with the line while his plane was in a holding pattern during a night arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-5) The song also features Toto members Steve Lukather, Jeff Porcaro and David Hungate.

# Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)
## Release
[edit]
The song "Minstrel Gigolo" served as the record's B-side, having previously backed Cross's debut single, "Ride Like the Wind".
Cross included "Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)" as a bonus track exclusive to cassette and CD versions of his 1983 album _Another Page_.

# Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)
A commercial success in the United States, it reached the top of both the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and Hot Adult Contemporary charts in October 1981, remaining at the top of the Hot 100 for three consecutive weeks. The song topped the VG-lista chart in Norway and was a top-ten hit in several other countries.

# Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)
## Background
[edit]
The song was written in collaboration between Cross, Burt Bacharach, and Bacharach's frequent writing partner and future wife Carole Bayer Sager. A fourth writing credit went to Liza Minnelli's ex-husband, Australian songwriter Peter Allen,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-British_Hit_Singles_&_Albums-3) a frequent collaborator with Bayer Sager. The line in the chorus "When you get caught between the moon and New York City" was taken from an unreleased song written by Allen and Bayer Sager.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-4) Allen came up with the line while his plane was in a holding pattern during a night arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-5) The song also features Toto members Steve Lukather, Jeff Porcaro and David Hungate.

# Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)
## Release
[edit]
The song "Minstrel Gigolo" served as the record's B-side, having previously backed Cross's debut single, "Ride Like the Wind".
Cross included "Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)" as a bonus track exclusive to cassette and CD versions of his 1983 album _Another Page_.

"**Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)**" is a song performed and co-written by American singer-songwriter Christopher Cross as the main theme for the 1981 film _Arthur_.
It was recognized as the year's Best Original Song at both the 54th Academy Awards and 39th Golden Globe Awards.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-British_Hit_Singles_&_Albums-3)

# Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)
A commercial success in the United States, it reached the top of both the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and Hot Adult Contemporary charts in October 1981, remaining at the top of the Hot 100 for three consecutive weeks. The song topped the VG-lista chart in Norway and was a top-ten hit in several other countries.

# Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)
## Background
[edit]
The song was written in collaboration between Cross, Burt Bacharach, and Bacharach's frequent writing partner and future wife Carole Bayer Sager. A fourth writing credit went to Liza Minnelli's ex-husband, Australian songwriter Peter Allen,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-British_Hit_Singles_&_Albums-3) a frequent collaborator with Bayer Sager. The line in the chorus "When you get caught between the moon and New York City" was taken from an unreleased song written by Allen and Bayer Sager.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-4) Allen came up with the line while his plane was in a holding pattern during a night arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur's_Theme_(Best_That_You_Can_Do)#cite_note-5) The song also features Toto members Steve Lukather, Jeff Porcaro and David Hungate.

# Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)
## Release
[edit]
The song "Minstrel Gigolo" served as the record's B-side, having previously backed Cross's debut single, "Ride Like the Wind".
Cross included "Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)" as a bonus track exclusive to cassette and CD versions of his 1983 album _Another Page_.

As a result of the CD price fixing issue, a settlement was reached in 2002 involving the music publishers and distributors Sony Music, WMG, Bertelsmann Music Group, EMI Music, and Universal Music. In restitution for price fixing they agreed to pay a $67.4 million fine and distribute $75.7 million in CDs to public and non-profit groups but admitted no wrongdoing.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-usatoday-54)
The "Big W" logo designed by Saul Bass, formerly used as the logo of Warner Bros. Entertainment, now used as the corporate logo of Warner Music Group

#### Warner Communications (1972–1990)
Looking to reduce its debt load from the AOL merger, Time Warner — the corporate successor to the original Time Warner Entertainment— sold Warner Music Group in 2004 to a group of investors led by [Edgar Bronfman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bronfman_Jr. "Edgar Bronfman Jr.") for US$2.6 billion. This spinoff was completed on February 27, 2004. In the 2004 transition to independent ownership, WMG hired record industry heavyweight Lyor Cohen from Universal Music Group (the result of the merger between the PolyGram and MCA label families) to attempt to reduce cost and increase performance. Time Warner (now Skydance) no longer retains any ownership in WMG, though it had the option to reacquire up to 20% of WMG for three years following the closing of the transaction. WMG did, however, have a royalty-free license to use the Warner Bros. shield for 15 years, as well as the old Warner Communications logo as WMG's main logo.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-55) With the expiration of the royalty-free license in May 2019, Warner Bros. Records (which became separate from the eponymous film studio after the spinoff) was renamed Warner Records and a new logo was introduced to replace the WB shield.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-56)
No longer a subsidiary of Time Warner, WMG began cutting costs by offloading loss-making or low-earning divisions. Like its rival EMI, Warner reacted to the growth of the digital music market by making a historic change, moving out of record production by closing or selling off disc-pressing plants, particularly in territories such as the US and the Netherlands, where production costs are high. The US manufacturing operations were sold to Cinram in 2003, before the purchase from Time Warner.

#### Warner Communications (1972–1990)
In 2005, the Miami-based Warner Bros. Publications, which printed and distributed a broad selection of sheet music, books, educational material, orchestrations, arrangements and tutorials, was sold to Alfred Music Publishing, although the sale excluded the print music business of WMG's Word Music (church hymnals, choral music and associated instrumental music).
On May 3, 2006, WMG apparently rejected a buyout offer from EMI.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-57) Then WMG offered to buy EMI and it also rejected the offer. In August 2007, EMI was purchased by Terra Firma Capital Partners.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-58) Talk of a possible WMG acquisition of EMI was fanned once again in 2009 after WMG executed a bond offering for $1.1 billion, which brought to light WMG's relatively strong financial position, which was contrasted with the weakened and debt-laden state of EMI.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-59) The same year WMG acquired Rykodisc and Roadrunner Records.
In September 2006, after pulling its content from the service earlier in the year, WMG entered into a new licensing deal with the video streaming service YouTube. Under the deal, WMG would be able to handle advertising sales for its artists' music videos on the service (as well as monetize user-created videos that include WMG-owned recordings) and partake in revenue sharing with YouTube, and also collaborate with YouTube on building a "premium" user experience for its content and associated channels.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-60)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-61)

#### Warner Communications (1972–1990)
On December 27, 2007, Warner announced that it would sell digital music without digital rights management through AmazonMP3, making it the third major label to do so.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-62) In 2008, _The New York Times_ reported that WMG's Atlantic Records became the first major record label to generate more than half of its music sales in the U.S. from digital products.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-63) In 2010, _Fast Company_ magazine detailed the company's transformation efforts in its recorded music division, where it has redefined the relationships it has with artists and diversified its revenue streams through its expansion into growing areas of the music business.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-64)
In 2008, WMG and several other major labels made investments in the new music streaming serviceSpotify.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-65)_[non-primary source needed_]
Due to licensing deal negotiations between Google and WMG in 2008, music video content licensed by WMG was removed from YouTube.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-67) In 2009, it was announced that the companies had reached a deal, and videos would be re-added to YouTube.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-68) As of 2017, WMG had extended its deal with YouTube.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-69)

#### Warner Communications (1972–1990)
In 2009, Warner Music took over its South-East Asian and Korean distribution of EMI audio and video products, including newer domestic releases, which was announced in September 2008. The two companies already enjoyed a successful partnership in India, the Middle East and North Africa, where EMI marketed and distributed Warner Music's physical product from 2005.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-70)
Leonard Blavatnik, founder of Access Industries, purchased WMG in 2011.
WMG formed a partnership with MTV Networks in June 2010 that allowed MTVN to exclusively sell ads on WMG's premium content; in turn, views of WMG videos would be counted as views for MTVN.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-71)

# Warner Music Group Names Val Blavatnik Managing Director of North America and U.K. Amid Other Executive Moves
### Jem Aswad
#### Latest
In a long-expected move, Warner Music Group has named Val Blavatnik Managing Director of North America, U.K. & Corporate Development amid several other top leadership moves. Blavatnik, 28, the son of Warner Music’s primary owner Len Blavatnik, will “unify and drive business and operational strategy across these markets while guiding the company’s investment strategy to support growth,” according to the announcement.
In other moves, Alejandro Duque is elevated to President, Warner Music International, adding the APAC and EMEA regions to his remit; Elliot Grainge is named Chairman of the independent distribution company ADA in the U.S. in addition to his current role as Chairman and CEO of Atlantic Music Group, and appoints longtime associate Zach Friedman to serve as Vice Chairman of ADA in addition to his COO role at AMG.

**Warner Music Group Corp.**,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-7) commonly abbreviated as **WMG**, is an American multinationalentertainment and record labelconglomerate headquartered in New York City. It is one of the "Big Four" recording companies and the third-largest in the global music industry, after Universal Music Group, Sony Music Group and BMG Rights Management.
texts.2: Formerly owned by Time Warner, the company sold WMG in 2004 to a group of private investors led by [Edgar Bronfman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bronfman_Jr. "Edgar Bronfman Jr."), in a move to alleviate Time Warner's debt load related to its merger with AOL. WMG was publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange from 2005 until 2011, when it announced its privatization and sale to Access Industries.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-:0-8) It later had its second IPO on Nasdaq in 2020, once again becoming a public company.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-:1-9) As of 2025, Access Industries remains the company's largest shareholder, owning 72% of the equity and controlling 98% of the voting power._[citation needed_] With a multibillion-dollar annual turnover, WMG employs more than 4,500 people and has operations in more than 50 countries throughout the world.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-Billboard_2011-07-20-10) The company owns and operates some of the largest and most successful record labels in the world, including Elektra, Reprise, Sire, Warner (formerly known as Warner Bros.), Parlophone (formerly owned by EMI), and Atlantic. WMG also owns Warner Chappell Music, one of the world's largest music publishers.

Evolution of Warner Music Group  
1928 By the end of the Silent Era, Jack Warner established a short-lived company called Music Publishers Holdings to oversee song rights for Warner Bros. films  
1958 Nearly thirty years later, Warner Bros. returned to the music business with the creation of Warner Bros. Records to ensure its musicians were contracted  
1963 Warner Records acquired Frank Sinatra's Reprise Records, and the labels were consolidated as Warner/Reprise  
1967 After Jack Warner sold his company, Warner Bros.-Seven Arts was formed; and it acquired Atlantic Records and established Warner Music Canada  
1968 Warner Bros.-Seven Arts Records, the rebranded Warner/Reprise, would lay the foundation for shared music distribution  
1970Kinney National Company acquired Elektra Records several months after buying Warner Bros., and established Kinney Record Group International  
1971Warner Music Group was established in its modern form with the separate Warner-Elektra-Atlantic labels being brought under one distribution network  
1972 Kinney divested its non-media assets into a separate company and renamed itself Warner Communications; it also purchased Asylum Records  
1978WEA Manufacturing was created to develop vinyl records and cassettes  
1981MTV was launched by Warner-Amex and it quickly became popular from songs by Warner-Elektra-Atlantic musicians  
1987Warner Chappell Music became Warner's music publisher after [Chappell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappell_&_Co. "Chappell & Co.") was acquired from PolyGram N.V.  
1988 Warner's international music footprint expanded with the purchase of the German record label, Teldec, and by 1991, Warner Classics was established  
1990Time Warner became the new parent company of Warner Music Group, and Warner Music Vision was formed as its primary music video distributor  
1995 Controversy with Interscope Records led to changes at the corporate level; several long-time music execs departed, such as Mo Ostin, Mike Fuchs, and Doug Morris  
2003[Edgar Bronfman Jr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bronfman_Jr. "Edgar Bronfman Jr."). led investors to acquire Warner Music from Time Warner, and he would serve as the company's CEO until 2011, overseeing its IPO
texts.27:
#### Warner Communications (1972–1990)
In 2000, Time Warner Entertainment merged with leading American internet service providerAOL to create AOL Time Warner, a new business entity. The new conglomerate again tried (and failed) to acquire EMI, and subsequent discussions about the takeover of BMG stalled, with Bertelsmann eventually offloading BMG into a joint venture with Sony. In 2002, AOL Time Warner further consolidated its hold over the publishing industry, buying 50% of music publisher Deston Songs from Edel AG. By the early 2000s, however, the effects of the dot-com crash had eroded AOL's profits and stock value, and with expected synergies between AOL and Time Warner never materializing, the Time Warner board sidelined its under-performing partner by dropping _AOL_ from its business name and reverting to TimeWarner.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-53)
As a result of the CD price fixing issue, a settlement was reached in 2002 involving the music publishers and distributors Sony Music, WMG, Bertelsmann Music Group, EMI Music, and Universal Music. In restitution for price fixing they agreed to pay a $67.4 million fine and distribute $75.7 million in CDs to public and non-profit groups but admitted no wrongdoing.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-usatoday-54)
The "Big W" logo designed by Saul Bass, formerly used as the logo of Warner Bros. Entertainment, now used as the corporate logo of Warner Music Group
texts.28:
#### Warner Communications (1972–1990)
Looking to reduce its debt load from the AOL merger, Time Warner — the corporate successor to the original Time Warner Entertainment— sold Warner Music Group in 2004 to a group of investors led by [Edgar Bronfman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bronfman_Jr. "Edgar Bronfman Jr.") for US$2.6 billion. This spinoff was completed on February 27, 2004. In the 2004 transition to independent ownership, WMG hired record industry heavyweight Lyor Cohen from Universal Music Group (the result of the merger between the PolyGram and MCA label families) to attempt to reduce cost and increase performance. Time Warner (now Skydance) no longer retains any ownership in WMG, though it had the option to reacquire up to 20% of WMG for three years following the closing of the transaction. WMG did, however, have a royalty-free license to use the Warner Bros. shield for 15 years, as well as the old Warner Communications logo as WMG's main logo.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-55) With the expiration of the royalty-free license in May 2019, Warner Bros. Records (which became separate from the eponymous film studio after the spinoff) was renamed Warner Records and a new logo was introduced to replace the WB shield.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-56)
No longer a subsidiary of Time Warner, WMG began cutting costs by offloading loss-making or low-earning divisions. Like its rival EMI, Warner reacted to the growth of the digital music market by making a historic change, moving out of record production by closing or selling off disc-pressing plants, particularly in territories such as the US and the Netherlands, where production costs are high. The US manufacturing operations were sold to Cinram in 2003, before the purchase from Time Warner.
texts.29:
#### Warner Communications (1972–1990)
In 2005, the Miami-based Warner Bros. Publications, which printed and distributed a broad selection of sheet music, books, educational material, orchestrations, arrangements and tutorials, was sold to Alfred Music Publishing, although the sale excluded the print music business of WMG's Word Music (church hymnals, choral music and associated instrumental music).
On May 3, 2006, WMG apparently rejected a buyout offer from EMI.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-57) Then WMG offered to buy EMI and it also rejected the offer. In August 2007, EMI was purchased by Terra Firma Capital Partners.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-58) Talk of a possible WMG acquisition of EMI was fanned once again in 2009 after WMG executed a bond offering for $1.1 billion, which brought to light WMG's relatively strong financial position, which was contrasted with the weakened and debt-laden state of EMI.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-59) The same year WMG acquired Rykodisc and Roadrunner Records.
In September 2006, after pulling its content from the service earlier in the year, WMG entered into a new licensing deal with the video streaming service YouTube. Under the deal, WMG would be able to handle advertising sales for its artists' music videos on the service (as well as monetize user-created videos that include WMG-owned recordings) and partake in revenue sharing with YouTube, and also collaborate with YouTube on building a "premium" user experience for its content and associated channels.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-60)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-61)
texts.30:
#### Warner Communications (1972–1990)
On December 27, 2007, Warner announced that it would sell digital music without digital rights management through AmazonMP3, making it the third major label to do so.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-62) In 2008, _The New York Times_ reported that WMG's Atlantic Records became the first major record label to generate more than half of its music sales in the U.S. from digital products.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-63) In 2010, _Fast Company_ magazine detailed the company's transformation efforts in its recorded music division, where it has redefined the relationships it has with artists and diversified its revenue streams through its expansion into growing areas of the music business.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-64)
In 2008, WMG and several other major labels made investments in the new music streaming serviceSpotify.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-65)_[non-primary source needed_]
Due to licensing deal negotiations between Google and WMG in 2008, music video content licensed by WMG was removed from YouTube.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-67) In 2009, it was announced that the companies had reached a deal, and videos would be re-added to YouTube.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-68) As of 2017, WMG had extended its deal with YouTube.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-69)
texts.31:
#### Warner Communications (1972–1990)
In 2009, Warner Music took over its South-East Asian and Korean distribution of EMI audio and video products, including newer domestic releases, which was announced in September 2008. The two companies already enjoyed a successful partnership in India, the Middle East and North Africa, where EMI marketed and distributed Warner Music's physical product from 2005.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-70)
Leonard Blavatnik, founder of Access Industries, purchased WMG in 2011.
WMG formed a partnership with MTV Networks in June 2010 that allowed MTVN to exclusively sell ads on WMG's premium content; in turn, views of WMG videos would be counted as views for MTVN.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-71)

In a long-expected move, Warner Music Group has named Val Blavatnik Managing Director of North America, U.K. & Corporate Development amid several other top leadership moves. Blavatnik, 28, the son of Warner Music’s primary owner Len Blavatnik, will “unify and drive business and operational strategy across these markets while guiding the company’s investment strategy to support growth,” according to the announcement.

**Warner Music Group Corp.**,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-7) commonly abbreviated as **WMG**, is an American multinationalentertainment and record labelconglomerate headquartered in New York City. It is one of the "Big Four" recording companies and the third-largest in the global music industry, after Universal Music Group, Sony Music Group and BMG Rights Management.

Formerly owned by Time Warner, the company sold WMG in 2004 to a group of private investors led by [Edgar Bronfman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Bronfman_Jr. "Edgar Bronfman Jr."), in a move to alleviate Time Warner's debt load related to its merger with AOL. WMG was publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange from 2005 until 2011, when it announced its privatization and sale to Access Industries.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-:0-8) It later had its second IPO on Nasdaq in 2020, once again becoming a public company.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-:1-9) As of 2025, Access Industries remains the company's largest shareholder, owning 72% of the equity and controlling 98% of the voting power._[citation needed_] With a multibillion-dollar annual turnover, WMG employs more than 4,500 people and has operations in more than 50 countries throughout the world.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group#cite_note-Billboard_2011-07-20-10) The company owns and operates some of the largest and most successful record labels in the world, including Elektra, Reprise, Sire, Warner (formerly known as Warner Bros.), Parlophone (formerly owned by EMI), and Atlantic. WMG also owns Warner Chappell Music, one of the world's largest music publishers.

Evolution of Warner Music Group  
1928 By the end of the Silent Era, Jack Warner established a short-lived company called Music Publishers Holdings to oversee song rights for Warner Bros. films  
1958 Nearly thirty years later, Warner Bros. returned to the music business with the creation of Warner Bros. Records to ensure its musicians were contracted  
1963 Warner Records acquired Frank Sinatra's Reprise Records, and the labels were consolidated as Warner/Reprise  
1967 After Jack Warner sold his company, Warner Bros.-Seven Arts was formed; and it acquired Atlantic Records and established Warner Music Canada  
1968 Warner Bros.-Seven Arts Records, the rebranded Warner/Reprise, would lay the foundation for shared music distribution
